text: A thin jet climbs into the night above Thailand.
No markings. No bombs. Just a pilot, a camera, and two long cases in its belly.
The pilot is Chuang. His unit is called the Black Cats.
Made by the CIA and Taiwan, the Black Cats fly the U-2.
A jet with the wings of a glider, near the edge of space.
China is about to test a hydrogen bomb.
Satellites can photograph the desert. But they cannot feel it.
So Chuang will fly three thousand kilometers, cross the bamboo curtain, and drop two listening posts into the sand near Lop Nur.
Each one is two meters long. It lands, and waits.
If the earth moves, it will tell Taipei.
On June seventeenth, a bomb called six-three-nine falls from an H-6.
Three point three megatons. The sky turns white.
Six weeks later, the sensors answer.
The signal is small. The meaning is not.
The flights end in 1974. The planes go home. The desert keeps the rest.
